Application Materials.content:
- A transcript: “We will need a transcript (in English or a certified translation) giving full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained.” Applicants should send scanned or certified copies of transcripts and **not** originals during the admissions process.
- English language proficiency results: applicants who are not nationals of a majority English-speaking country “will need to submit evidence of your proficiency in English to the UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) and University's required standards.”
- One completed reference: applicants should check whether one or two references are required for the programme. They should supply at least one reference from an academic referee able to comment on academic work and suitability for postgraduate study; where this is not possible, references from other sources such as an employer or colleague may be accepted. References from family members, partners or spouses are not accepted. References for postgraduate applications must be in **pdf format, on headed paper, dated, signed/stamped and recommend you for your chosen programme**. If sent directly by the referee, it must come from their institutional or company email address and may be sent to [pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk) with the student reference number, name and programme of study.
- Personal statement: not all programmes require one, but applicants may provide one. Guidance says to tailor it to the course, explain how the course links past and future, show abilities and fit with the course, provide evidence of skills, commitment and enthusiasm, explain reasons for studying the course at the University of Exeter, and include particular interest in the subject. It should **stick to under 500 words**, use short clear sentences, may use headings such as “Why the University of Exeter?”, “Why this course?”, and “Career plans”, and use a standard font such as Arial or Times New Roman, text size 11.
- Essential documentation for an initial decision on taught programme applications: applicants should send as many required supporting documents as possible with the application. As a **minimum**, they need to complete the Module Information section of the application form with details of outstanding modules and expected completion date, and send any interim transcripts available to support the application.
- Supporting documentation after application: the University recommends uploading all supporting documents with the application, but applicants can apply before completing all academic qualifications and will need to provide any interim transcripts available.
- International students: if academic or English language qualifications are not yet complete, an offer may be made conditional on completing these and supplying any required references. International students must provide documentary evidence that conditions have been met before an offer can be considered unconditional. Original copies are not required at the application stage.

Interview Requirements.content: Applicants may be interviewed by video conference to assess their programming ability and suitability for the course.

Application Deadlines.content:
Teaching starts for most programmes in late September.
**International applicants:** For international applicants wishing to join in 2026/2027 the application deadline is **23:59 Friday 11 September 2026** UK time.
January start date: applications to apply for programmes that start in January 2027 will open on **Monday 2 March 2026** and close at **23:59 Monday 4 January 2027**.
The University advises international applicants to submit a complete application by **mid-July** for September start.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Normally a 2:1 degree or equivalent**.
- Applicants are required to have **at least a 2:1 degree in a strongly numerate subject** (e.g. computer science, mathematics or physics) and must be able to show **evidence of good programming ability in a recognised modern computer language**.
- You do **not need a computing background**.
- Applicants may be interviewed by video conference to assess their programming ability and suitability for the course.
- The Python programming language is used extensively during this course and applicants with experience in other languages will be asked to **learn basic Python before commencing the course**.
- The University may consider applications with non-standard qualifications where there is evidence of exceptional performance in modules relevant to the programme of study, significant relevant work experience, or relevant professional qualifications.
- For applicants from China: applicants for postgraduate taught programmes need a bachelor’s degree certificate and graduation certificate from a domestic university recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education, with grades equivalent to the UK 2:1 or 2:2 depending on the course requirement. For 2026 entry, **UK 2:1 = 75%** for Chinese undergraduate qualifications. The previous domestic university ranking requirement has been removed; all Chinese universities use a unified score standard, and all undergraduate institutions on the official Chinese Ministry of Education recognised list are accepted. Some courses may have additional undergraduate subject-background requirements.

Program Overview.content:
The MSc Cyber Security Analytics is a **1 year full-time** programme at **Streatham Campus**. It is for applicants with a degree in a strongly numerate subject and an interest in a career in cyber security, data analytics, or the intersection of both; a computing background is not required.
- The programme is taught in a multi-disciplinary partnership of Computer Science, the University of Exeter Business School and the Law School, with input from leading industry experts.
- Exeter works closely with the local cyber security community, including the [South West Cyber Security Cluster](https://southwestcsc.org/) and [BSides Exeter](https://bsidesexeter.co.uk/community/).
- Students learn how to recognise and manage risks to a network or system’s security with data analytics, and how to build and defend secure systems with cyber security.
- The course investigates wider security elements including mathematical, human and societal factors, with the option to study cyber security law and the future of virtual currency.
The MSc Cyber Security Analytics allows students to study two highly sought after skills: cyber security and data science. This combination enables students to study challenges in modern life from two complementary viewpoints. The course has a strong focus on ensuring that safety, security and data privacy are inherent in the design of software systems. Compulsory modules provide a foundation in cyber security and data science, while optional module choices allow students to create a degree that matches their interests.
MSc Cyber Security Analytics consists of core compulsory Cyber Security and Data Analytics focused modules worth 60 credits, a 60-credit MSc Research project, and 60 credits of optional modules: two chosen from Cyber modules and two from Data Science / Analytics. The research project typically applies knowledge of both cyber security and data analytics and is supervised by a research expert in the student’s chosen area. The full-time programme starts in September, taught elements are concluded by May, and research continues until September. A part-time two-year route is also available starting in September.
As academic partners of the Chartered Institute of Information Security, MSc students are eligible for free student membership, enabling them to develop their network, make contacts within the cyber security community, attend CIISec events and contribute articles to their magazine. Exeter’s long-established partnership with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/institutes/idsai/turinginstitute/), the UK’s national institute for data science and artificial intelligence, provides strong connections to the UK data science and AI research community. The University currently hosts 11 Turing Fellows and one Turing AI Fellow; lectures, conferences and seminars organised by Turing and the Turing University Network are usually open to students in person or online.
Computer science students use world-class spacious teaching labs designed for comfortable, collaborative working in a sensory-friendly environment. The University has invested £50 million in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence capabilities through the [Accelerating Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (ADA) project](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/projectada/), which has invested in teaching, research and infrastructure that this programme benefits from.
Teaching is mainly delivered by lectures, workshops and online materials. Industry connections and local, national and international cyber security networks inform the curriculum, which is regularly reviewed to support the employability of MSc students. Students are taught by experts active in research and practice; academic staff are active in internationally recognised research across a wide range of topics. Exeter’s Security and Trust of Advanced Systems group focuses on building secure, safe, privacy-preserving, reliable and trustworthy systems, and students can also engage with data science research through the [Institute for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/institutes/idsai/).
Cyber security and data science affect almost every aspect of society, and companies worldwide need cyber security experts. The programme provides foundations for careers in data analytics, cyber security, or the intersection of both. Graduate opportunities span sectors including software engineering, health communications, education, life sciences, finance, civil service, intelligence and manufacturing. The programme is particularly suited to professionals and graduates looking to develop career options or pursue academia. Students receive support from the dedicated Career Zone team, including one-on-one guidance, business and industry contacts, training events, workshops and lectures.

Curriculum.content:
Duration: **1 year full time**. Campus: **Streatham Campus**.
The MSc Cyber Security Analytics consists of core compulsory Cyber Security and Data Analytics focussed modules worth **60 credits**, a **60-credit MSc Research project**, and **60 credits of optional modules** (two chosen from Cyber modules and two from Data Science / Analytics). The full time programme starts in September and the taught elements are concluded by May. Research continues until September. Part-time study over two years also begins in September: in year one students study at least 4 modules, which must include ECMM443 Introduction to Data Science, ECMM462 Fundamentals of Security, and COMM108 Data Systems; in year two students complete at least 4 modules, including ECMM463 Building Secure and Trustworthy Systems if not already taken in year 1, and complete the research project.
Modules: **120 credits of compulsory modules, 60 credits of optional modules**. Students must select **30 credits of Cyber Optional modules and 30 credits of Data Science/Analytics modules**.

Cost of Attendance.content:
For international students, the University estimates that a single student living in Exeter or Cornwall will need approximately **£1,300-£2,000 a month** to meet basic living expenses such as accommodation (rent), transport, food and drink, entertainment, utility bills, clothes and socialising.
| Expense | Average cost per week* |
| --- | --- |
| Student halls (bills included) | £150-£270 (self-catered); £250-£345 (catered) |
| Rooms in private accommodation (without bills) | £135-£250 |
| Household bills (gas, electricity, water, broadband & a TV licence) | £30 |
| Groceries | £60 |
| Socialising (dining out, going to cafes & bars) | £40 |
| Public transport | £18 |
| Mobile phone bill (SIM only plan) | £4.50 |
| Student gym membership | £15 |
| **Total** | **£316 - £421/week estimate** |
*Based on average local spend April 2026.
As an approximate estimate for a single person living in shared accommodation, household bills per month are: gas £55 - £75, electricity £65-£85, internet £25 - £35, water £30-£40. A TV Licence costs £13.25 per month.

Financial Aid.content:
Exeter Excellence Scholarships 2026/27 - Postgraduate Taught (Masters), Round 2 - September 2026 entry only: awards of **£3,000, £5,000 or £10,000** are offered by departments including **Environment, Science and Economy - Computer Science**. All campus-based Postgraduate taught degrees (Masters) in the listed areas are eligible, except specified ineligible programmes; fully online or distance learning programmes are not eligible.
You can apply if you:
- have International fee status (including any EU applicants required to pay International fees in 2026/27)
- already hold an offer (conditional or unconditional) to study an eligible Postgraduate taught degree at the University of Exeter, beginning in September 2026. These scholarships are intended for self-funded students.
Scholarship recipients are selected on academic merit, based on the Masters programme application; applicants will typically be expected to demonstrate that they have achieved or are able to achieve the equivalent of UK upper second class degree (2:1). Selection also considers academic and career ambitions, a clear plan for making the most of the study opportunity, social responsibility, and willingness to engage with the Exeter community.
To be considered, once you have your programme offer, apply using the webform [here](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/SwA753Y8uM). A personal statement of no more than 300 words is required. The deadline for Round 2 is **1 July 2026 (23:59 British Summer Time)**. Eligible offer holders who apply in Round 2 will be notified within one month of applying and no later than **16 July 2026**.
These scholarships are awarded as a reduction in the first-year International tuition fees, do not recur for subsequent years of study, and can be combined with a University of Exeter Postgraduate Taught Scholarship 2026/27 for Bangladesh, Canada, China (mainland), India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Nepal, Pakistan, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand, Türkiye or Vietnam to a maximum award value of **£10,000**. Full Terms and Conditions are available [here](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/v8media/universityofexeter/funding/documents/Important-info-TsCs-Exeter-Excellence-PGT-2026-27.pdf).

Multiple Applications.content: No. When you accept your place on a programme you are committing to that specific programme. Any other offers you may be holding will be released.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Requests for deferral will be considered on a case by case basis. Applicants wishing to defer will need to put their request in writing and [submit it via our enquiry form](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/enquiry/) (please ensure you quote your Exeter Reference Number – which can be found on the top of your original offer email). We aim to notify applicants of an outcome within **10 working days**. Applicants are only permitted to defer entry once. Subsequent to this, a new application will be required which will be considered in line with others applying for entry in that year.
| Start date | Deadline |
| --- | --- |
| Programmes commencing in September | **30 September** |
| All other start dates | **Within 4 weeks of the start date of your programme** |
Applicants who do not request a deferral within this timeframe will be required to reapply, as your original application and documentation will not be retained.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Your offer will be either **Conditional** or **Unconditional**:
- **Conditional** means that you have not yet satisfied academic, English language or any other entry requirements. Details of offer conditions and how to satisfy these requirements, including [paying your deposit](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/fees/tuition-fee-deposit/), will be given in the offer letter.
- For a **full-time taught postgraduate programme**, applicants need to pay the deposit to secure their place and should pay by the deadline even if they have not yet met all the conditions of the offer.
- The deadline for meeting all conditions is normally **31 August** for September entry. Applicants must supply required documentation showing they have met outstanding academic requirements, English language and/or references, or inform Exeter by **31 August** what conditions remain and when they expect to meet them.
- If Exeter does not hear from the applicant by **31 August** and outstanding conditions remain, the University reserves the right to **withdraw or defer the application to the following year**.
- To receive a formal unconditional offer letter and, where needed, a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies for a Student Visa, applicants must meet: academic conditions by providing degree certificates, transcripts and references as explained in the Conditional offer letter; non-academic conditions such as a [DBS](http://www.exeter.ac.uk/dbs/) check; and the required English language standard by providing an English language test certificate meeting [Exeter’s requirements](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/).
- Offer holders who successfully complete a [Pre-Sessional English course at the University of Exeter International Study Centre](https://www.exeterisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english) and meet the requirements for progression to their chosen degree are not required to undertake an additional IELTS or TOEFL test. Exeter does not accept pre-sessional courses delivered by other INTO centres or organisations.
